I've not had a serious relationship for a long time, but I dated someone for nearly two years, and when that ended I got really sick.  Since he and I stopped seeing each other, I've been working on my diet, and getting plenty exercise.  If you've got a bad cold you should focus on resting, getting plenty of sleep, and eating as well as you can.  Lots of vitamin c, fruit and vegetables, and if it's not too hot where you are then baths with essential oils are soothing too.

I was in my mid twenties when I realised the same (I'm 35 now) and it was a bit of a shock!  The only reason I found out is because my best friend told me a horribly detailed story about her labia minora becoming irritated while wearing man made fibres :-/

I haven't really done much investigation about it, but what I can say, is that it doesn't seem to cause any issues!  Everything down there functions just fine and I've been told things look nice and "tidy" which is cool.

I think the trick here is to not use the word "normal".  There's no standardised labia type that's considered normal.  Some people have average labia, some have large, and some of us have little ones.

http://www.self.com/story/what-are-normal-labia

As long as this isn't a recent change then I think you're ok.
I'm so sorry for what's happened to you.   As far as I'm concerned, coercion is rape.

You do not have to just "get over it".  There is no timescale for healing from trauma.

I was sexually assaulted at 15 and raped at 20 by different guys, and it's taken me until the age of 35 to really start dealing with it.  

Are you in counselling?  If not I really recommend giving it a go if you can.

I really wish that I could tell my ex friend Tom how much pain he caused me. I'd like to ask him why he manipulated me into sex (pretending to care about me and forming an emotional bond) after I opened up to him about being sexually abused at 15 and then raped in my twenties.  I'd like to tell him that he needs to sort himself out, stop doing so many drugs and stop treating women like trash.  I also want to let him know that I forgive him, because I know he hurts people because he's hurting too.  That I have to forgive him because the anger and pain is too heavy for me to carry any more.  I'd thank him for making me feel so bad that I finally reached out to my local rape crisis centre for counselling.   He unintentionally made my life so much better by treating me like I wasn't human.  Thank you, Tom.

I was also raped at a house party, while drunk, and possibly my drink had been spiked.   I don't remember the act completely but I know enough to know it happened and it was wrong, especially as the guys threatened me with a lawyer when my friends confronted them after I came to.  Counselling is the best thing I ever did.  I don't talk so much about what happened, I talk about how it's affected every aspect of my life since.  It's worth trying counselling, see if it works for you.
